implementerProof.how: This round changed the refusal itself, so every claim behind it was measured against real jj 0.45.1 rather than read. (a) `.jj` as a regular file: `jj status` below a directory holding one answers `Error: There is no jj repo in "."`, so narrowing the walk to a `.jj` directory matches jj and refusing it would have refused a run jj carries out with no repository in sight. (b) `.jj` as a symlink to a real repository's `.jj`: jj opens it (`jj status` reports that repository's working copy), so following symlinks with os.Stat is the right read — and production refuses such an ancestor, measured on the CLI, with the repository untouched. (c) The comment's new claim that -R does not fence jj off the repository its working directory sits in: `jj -R <target> log` run inside another repository migrated that repository's configuration and wrote `config-id` into it, exactly as claimed. (d) The safety that rests on (c): a PATH-shim trace of every child of one real provision run shows 12 jj children, the 11 with a -R each running in its own -R directory and the one rootless `jj git init --colocate` running under the guard. (e) The tester's round-1 red test was folded into TestProvisionLeavesTheEnclosingRepositoryUntouched as a row and its file deleted; the row is a genuine pin, not a formality: with refuseEnclosingWorkspace's walk made lexical again in a scratch copy, that row and only that row fails. (f) The whole module, the CLI from inside the pod's workspace, the shim trace and merged-root-waits.sh were all re-run at this head.

observations: Round 2's observation is closed: the refusal now reads 'refusing to run jj in <the path named>, which resolves to <the path jj stands in>: <repository>/.jj is a Jujutsu repository …'.

Not a failure, for the reviewer to weigh: this round made following symlinks load-bearing — os.Lstat became os.Stat so that a `.jj` which is a symlink to a repository's `.jj` still counts — and jj does open such a directory (measured: `jj status` below it reports that repository's working copy). Production refuses it, measured on the CLI with the repository untouched. Nothing pins it: TestAJJThatCreatesARepositoryIsRefusedInsideOne has rows for a repository, a grandparent, a regular file named `.jj`, a repository not there yet and no repository, and none for a `.jj` symlink. A change back to os.Lstat would pass every row while jj still opened and wrote that repository. One table row closes it, beside the regular-file row it belongs with.
